names.name: Jimmies
names.said: Boston and Philadelphia say jimmies. Say it in Los Angeles and you get a blank look.

text.what: The long rod-shaped sprinkles, above all the chocolate ones. The tiny balls are nonpareils.
text.story:
Jimmies is the most popular term for chocolate sprinkles in Boston, Philadelphia and New England. The origin is uncertain; it is first documented in 1930, as a cake topping. The Just Born Candy Company of Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, says it invented the product and named them after an employee.

A second story credits Sidney Farber's Jimmy Fund and Brigham's ice cream, which charged a penny extra for chocolate sprinkles to benefit it — but the fund started in 1948, well after the word is first recorded. Nonpareils go back to at least the late eighteenth century, as decoration for pièces montées.
